## What a model can do

[`Caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps) describes
what a model can be sent and what it can send back. A modality is one of
`text`, `image`, `audio` or `video`.
[`Caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps) holds three
tuples of modalities. Accepting images and producing images are separate
abilities, so each has its own tuple.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Field</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>inp</code></td>
<td>The modalities the model accepts</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>out</code></td>
<td>The modalities the model returns in an ordinary reply</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>tools</code></td>
<td>The modalities the model returns only when you give it a generation
tool that the provider runs, such as the OpenAI image generation
tool</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>source</code></td>
<td>Where the answer came from</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The `source` field has one of these values: `fastllm`, `fallback`,
`mmproj`, `config`, `runtime` or `default`. The value `default` means
that nothing knew the answer. A `default`
[`Caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps) means the
modalities are unknown. It does not mean text only. `known` is `False`
for a `default`
[`Caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps), so a caller
can tell the two cases apart.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Member</th>
<th>Result</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>accepts(kind)</code></td>
<td><code>True</code> when <code>kind</code> is in <code>inp</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>gen_image</code>, <code>gen_video</code></td>
<td><code>True</code> when the kind is in <code>out</code> or in
<code>tools</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>fmt()</code></td>
<td>A short line for a status bar. It is empty for a text-in, text-out
model, and <code>'modalities unknown'</code> when <code>known</code> is
<code>False</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### Caps

``` python
def Caps(
    inp:tuple=('text',), out:tuple=('text',), tools:tuple=(), source:str='default'
)->None:
```

*What a model can be sent, and what it can send back.*

``` python
c = Caps(('text', 'image'), ('text',), source='fastllm')
test_eq((c.accepts('image'), c.accepts('audio')), (True, False))
test_eq((c.gen_image, c.known), (False, True))
test_eq(c.fmt(), 'in: text image')
test_eq(repr(c), 'Caps(in=text+image, out=text, fastllm)')
```

``` python
test_eq(Caps().known, False)
test_eq(Caps().fmt(), 'modalities unknown')
test_eq(Caps(source='fastllm').fmt(), '')
test_eq(Caps(tools=('image',), source='fastllm').gen_image, True)
```

## Hosted models

The fastllm package ships a table of model facts. The table describes
the modalities of a model in one of three ways. A fourth entry, the
endpoint list, sets `tools`.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Table entry</th>
<th><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps"><code>Caps</code></a>
that <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#tbl_caps"><code>tbl_caps</code></a>
builds</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Lists of input and output modalities</td>
<td><code>inp</code> and <code>out</code> from the lists</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A <code>supports_vision</code> flag</td>
<td><code>inp</code> is <code>('text', 'image')</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A <code>mode</code> such as <code>image_generation</code></td>
<td><code>out</code> from the mode, for a model that only generates</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The <code>/v1/responses</code> endpoint in
<code>supported_endpoints</code></td>
<td><code>tools</code> is <code>('image',)</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`tbl_caps(model)` returns a
[`Caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps) with
`source='fastllm'`. It returns `None` when the table has nothing about
the model.
[`tool_modalities`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#tool_modalities)
finds the `tools` value from `ENDPOINT_TOOLS`. A model name can carry a
vendor prefix, as in `openai/gpt-5.1`.

### tool_modalities

``` python
def tool_modalities(
    info
):
```

*The modalities a model can produce through a provider-run tool, from
its `supported_endpoints`.*

``` python
c = tbl_caps('gpt-5.1')
test_eq(({'text', 'image'} <= set(c.inp), c.out, c.source), (True, ('text', 'image'), 'fastllm'))   # newer tables add inputs such as pdf
test_eq(c.tools, ('image',))              # it serves /v1/responses, so it can be told to draw
```

``` python
from unittest.mock import patch
with patch('fastllm.types.get_model_info', lambda m, p=None: {'mode': 'chat', 'supports_vision': True}):
    test_eq(tbl_caps('x').inp, ('text', 'image'))      # only `supports_vision` was set
test_eq({'text', 'image', 'audio', 'video'} <= set(tbl_caps('gemini-2.5-pro').inp), True)   # newer tables add pdf
test_eq(tbl_caps('gpt-image-1').out, ('image',))      # read off `mode`, not the output list
test_eq(tbl_caps('no-such-model-anywhere'), None)
```

The table can lack a recent model. `fallback_caps(model)` covers vendors
whose models all read images. It checks whether the lowercased name
contains a key of `CAPS_FALLBACK`: `claude`, `anthropic/`, `sonnet`,
`opus`, `haiku` or `fable`. A match gives text and image input with
`source='fallback'`. No match gives `None`.

`hosted_caps(model)` is the function to call for a hosted model. It
tries
[`tbl_caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#tbl_caps),
then
[`fallback_caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#fallback_caps).
It returns an unknown
[`Caps()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps) when both
return `None`.

### fallback_caps

``` python
def fallback_caps(
    model
):
```

*The [`Caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps) for a
model whose name matches a prefix in `CAPS_FALLBACK`, or None.*

``` python
test_eq(fallback_caps('claude-opus-4-1').inp, ('text', 'image'))
test_eq(fallback_caps('gpt-5.1'), None)               # the table already covers it
test_eq(hosted_caps('gpt-5.1').source, 'fastllm')
test_eq(hosted_caps('claude-sonnet-4-5').source, 'fastllm')   # the table knows this one
test_eq(hosted_caps('claude-opus-99').source, 'fallback')     # ...but not this one
test_eq(hosted_caps('no-such-model-anywhere').source, 'default')
```

The context window of a model is the number of tokens that the model can
read at once. `hosted_ctx(model)` reads it from the same table. It uses
`max_input_tokens` when that value is nonzero. Otherwise it tries
`max_tokens`. It returns `(tokens, note)`.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Table result</th>
<th><code>tokens</code></th>
<th><code>note</code></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>A window is listed</td>
<td>The window</td>
<td><code>''</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>No window, or the lookup raises an error</td>
<td><code>DFLT_CTX</code> (128,000), or the <code>dflt</code> you
pass</td>
<td>Text that says the window is unknown and gives the assumed size, so
you can show it to the user</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/caps.py#L93"

### hosted_ctx

``` python
def hosted_ctx(
    model, dflt:int=128000
):
```

*The context window of a hosted model as `(tokens, note)`, where `note`
says when the figure is assumed.*

``` python
n, note = hosted_ctx('gpt-5.1')
assert n > 100_000 and note == ''
n, note = hosted_ctx('no-such-model-anywhere')
test_eq((n, note), (DFLT_CTX, 'context window unknown, assuming 128k'))
test_eq(hosted_ctx('no-such-model-anywhere', dflt=8192)[0], 8192)
```

## Local models

A local model is named by a file path or by a Hugging Face repository
id. `is_path(model)` returns `True` for a path. A name that ends in
`.gguf` or `.litertlm` is a path, and so is any name that exists on
disk. `hub_files(repo)` lists the files of a repository that are in the
local Hugging Face cache. It does not use the network. It returns `[]`
when the repository is not cached.

A GGUF model reads images only when an `mmproj` file comes with it. An
`mmproj` file is a projector that converts pictures into input that the
language model reads. `mmproj_caps(model, model_path)` looks for a
`.gguf` file with `mmproj` in its name. It searches the cached
repository and the folder of `model_path`. It also searches the folder
of `model` when `model` is a path. It returns image input with
`source='mmproj'` when it finds one. It returns `None` otherwise.

### is_path

``` python
def is_path(
    model
):
```

*True when `model` names a local file or path instead of a Hugging Face
repo id.*

``` python
test_eq(is_path('model.gguf'), True)
test_eq(is_path('google/gemma-3-4b-it'), False)
test_eq(is_path(''), False)
test_eq(is_path('.'), True)            # an existing path, whatever it is named
```

``` python
import tempfile
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    (Path(d)/'qwen3-4b-Q4_K_M.gguf').touch()
    test_eq(mmproj_caps(None, f'{d}/qwen3-4b-Q4_K_M.gguf'), None)     # text-only
    (Path(d)/'mmproj-F16.gguf').touch()
    test_eq(mmproj_caps(None, f'{d}/qwen3-4b-Q4_K_M.gguf').inp, ('text', 'image'))
```

MLX and Transformers models describe themselves in a `config.json` file.
A model with a vision or audio encoder has a key for it in that file.

`read_cfg(model, model_path)` loads the file from a local folder or from
the Hugging Face cache. It returns `{}` when the file is missing or
unreadable.

`cfg_caps(model, model_path)` returns a
[`Caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps) with
`source='config'`, or `None` when
[`read_cfg`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#read_cfg)
returns `{}`. Text is always an input. The table shows the keys that add
an input modality.

</tr>
<tr>


*A model’s `config.json` as a dict, from a local folder or the hub
cache, else `{}`.*

``` python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    (Path(d)/'config.json').write_text('{"model_type": "qwen3"}')
    test_eq(cfg_caps(None, d).inp, ('text',))
    (Path(d)/'config.json').write_text('{"vision_config": {}, "audio_config": {}}')
    test_eq(cfg_caps(None, d).inp, ('text', 'image', 'audio'))
```

``` python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    (Path(d)/'config.json').write_text('not json')
    test_eq(read_cfg(None, d), {})
    test_eq(cfg_caps(None, d), None)
test_eq(cfg_caps(None, '/nonexistent/path'), None)
```
